metadata.title: High Velocity Runaway Binaries from Supernovae in Triple Systems

evidence.quote: Gaia DR2 1540013339194597376, which can be identified to be a HVS candidate via its proper motion of 900 km/s alone (Bromley et al. 2018)
hypervelocity stars (HVSs), stars which have velocities in the Galactic reference frame that are high enough to achieve escape velocity

Upon visual inspection of HVS candidates, it is found that several lie on this “binary main sequence”, including but not necessarily limited to Gaia DR2 1540013339194597376, which can be identified to be a HVS candidate via its proper motion of 900 km/s alone (Bromley et al. 2018), and Gaia DR2 1976597452042003072, with a proper motion of 500 km/s.
Gaia DR2 1976597452042003072, with a proper motion of 500 km/s
hypervelocity stars (HVSs), stars which have velocities in the Galactic reference frame that are high enough to achieve escape velocity

Upon visual inspection of HVS candidates, it is found that several lie on this “binary main sequence”, including but not necessarily limited to Gaia DR2 1540013339194597376, which can be identified to be a HVS candidate via its proper motion of 900 km/s alone (Bromley et al. 2018), and Gaia DR2 1976597452042003072, with a proper motion of 500 km/s.

notes: Gaia DR2 1540013339194597376 and Gaia DR2 1976597452042003072 are the only individually identified stars; both occur in the introduction as pre-existing HVS candidates discussed as possible unresolved binaries on the binary main sequence (T:p1-b13). The paper does not perform a dedicated Galactic-boundness analysis for either. The first has an explicit Bromley et al. (2018) attribution; the second appears in the same HVS-candidate list without a separate discovery citation. The paper's km/s values for “proper motion” are reproduced as stated.

Gaia DR2 1540013339194597376: At T:p1-b13 the paper states that Gaia DR2 1540013339194597376 "can be identified to be a HVS candidate via its proper motion of 900 km/s alone (Bromley et al. 2018)". This is a total proper-motion speed, not the equatorial proper-motion components proper_motion_ra/proper_motion_dec, so it cannot be assigned to either component quantity under the stated definitions. No other position, distance, parallax, velocity, Galactocentric, or bound/unbound probability values are reported for this star.

Gaia DR2 1976597452042003072: In T:p1-b13 the paper states: "Gaia DR2 1976597452042003072, with a proper motion of 500 km/s." This is a total transverse speed quoted in velocity units, not a component-resolved angular proper motion (mas/yr, arcsec/yr, etc.), and the paper does not report separate proper-motion components, position, distance, parallax, or radial velocity for this star. Because the only reported value is a single total proper-motion-equivalent speed, it cannot be assigned to proper_motion_ra or proper_motion_dec, and no other listed quantity is reported for this star.
